fieldValues.title: Affirmation by fork duplicates 304 records: 97% of affirmed records are copies of a suggestion
fieldValues.summary: Measured on srs-programme master, 2026-10-30. Of 1,585 typed records, 313 are in Affirmed; 304 of them are copies of a suggestion that stays in Suggestions, joined by derived-from. Every reader must resolve each pair to the right copy, and every reference must choose one.
evidence: Per type, suggested / affirmed / pairs: problem 137/133/133, remedy 61/53/53, cluster 24/24/24, persona-in-domain 18/18/18, domain 17/15/15, tension 47/19/18, principle 28/13/13, pole 94/18/16, axis-in-domain 12/12/9, persona 5/5/5
Still waiting as suggestion only: 78 poles, 29 tensions, 15 principles, 8 remedies, 31 findings (findings are not affirmed by design)
Every one of the 24 clusters was forked into Affirmed, though the owner says clusters rarely need affirmation (vignette 8b9b1066)

Building the research threads on 2026-10-30, each cited problem, remedy and domain had to be checked for which copy was affirmed: SP-24, SP-48, SP-86, SP-09, SP-22, SP-116 to SP-119, remedy 364126da, 13 domains; two flow stages have no affirmed copy at all
srs-rust#1490 cited SP-116 for the data dump (it is SP-119): a label resolved against the wrong record
fieldValues.body: Gathered for the research thread on affirmation and confidence. The fork-and-copy mechanism (handbook: Suggested, affirmed, set aside; canon() follows derived-from) makes the human layer a second copy of the data rather than a judgement on the first. The owner (2026-10-30): "These are a strange overhead and they introduce weird complexity. We have duplicate records."
